# HMessageScroller

> Variable-height message scrolling with reading-position preservation and jump-to-latest.

[Start with the Hearth UI agent index](../../../llms.txt). This describes repository source for version 0.10.0. Match documentation to your installed source/release.

## Identity

- Vue export: `HMessageScroller` from `@hearth-ui/vue`.
- Custom element: `<hearth-message-scroller>`.
- Constructor: `HearthMessageScrollerElement` from `@hearth-ui/elements`.
- Category: Layouts.
- [Implementation](https://github.com/samishal1998/hearth-ui/blob/main/src/components/HMessageScroller.vue).

## Choose and use it correctly

- Use stable direct child elements as messages (Vue keys or persistent custom-element hosts). Native scrolling and ResizeObserver follow new/streaming content while at the end; scrolling away pauses follow. A retained visible child anchors reading position when history is prepended. Jump to latest resumes follow.
- This is a variable-height scroll container, not virtualization or a log announcer. Keep live announcements in an application-owned status. Wrapper elements grouping all messages into one child reduce prepend anchoring precision. follow is controlled through update:follow; default true.

## Public API

label, maxHeight: string · follow: boolean

A `?` marks optional source props. Props with defaults may be omitted. Internal `formDisabled` and `control-sync` plumbing is excluded below; do not use it in application code.

```ts
type Props = {
    label: string;
    follow?: boolean;
    maxHeight?: string;
};
```

### Defaults

```ts
{ follow: true, maxHeight: "480px" }
```

### Events

update:follow(boolean)

```ts
type Emits = {
    "update:follow": [
        follow: boolean
    ];
};
```

Vue-emitted custom-element events expose argument arrays in `event.detail`. Listen on the element. Native events such as `click` retain their normal payloads. The elements package provides framework-independent DOM event types.

### Slots

default

Vue uses `<template #slotName>`; custom elements use `<div slot="slotName">`. Web components do not support Vue scoped slots.

### CSS parts

base, viewport, content

Use `hearth-message-scroller::part(part-name)` for an exposed part or inherited `--h-*` tokens for shared styling. Native Vue components use the shared stylesheet and `h-*` classes.

## Vue example

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { HMessageScroller, HMessage } from '@hearth-ui/vue';
import '@hearth-ui/vue/styles.css';

</script>

<template>
  <HMessageScroller label="Conversation" max-height="240px"><HMessage author="User">Can you check the build?</HMessage><HMessage author="Assistant">The build passed.</HMessage></HMessageScroller>
</template>
```

## Web-component example

Provide a mount point. For field submission, use an owning native form; the auth page already contains its own form.

```html
<div id="example"></div>
```

This is bundler-based ESM. For raw HTML, load `dist/themes.css` with a link and import `registerElements` from `./dist/elements/index.js` instead. Initial array/object properties are assigned before connection to establish reset defaults.

```js
import { registerElements } from '@hearth-ui/elements';
import '@hearth-ui/elements/themes.css';
registerElements();

const mount = document.querySelector('#example');
const element = document.createElement('hearth-message-scroller');
Object.assign(element, {
  "label": "Conversation",
  "maxHeight": "240px"
});

element.innerHTML = "<hearth-message author=\"User\">Can you check the build?</hearth-message><hearth-message author=\"Assistant\">The build passed.</hearth-message>"; // Static example markup only; never inject untrusted HTML.

element.addEventListener('update:follow', event => {
  const [value] = event.detail;
  // Update your application state using value.
});

mount.append(element);
```
